subject: Non-learning certification, export lifecycle & subprocessor attestations
messages:
From: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@halcyon.ai>
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@halcyon.ai>, procurement@halcyon.ai
Date: Mon, 10 Sep 2028 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: initial ask: confirmation on no-model-learning and evidence pack

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency and cost profile look promising for our agent workflows. Procurement asked me to get the privacy/security confirmations in writing before we proceed to legal redlines. Two specific asks: a) a firm no-model-learning commitment for Halcyon-enterprise interactions (no training or fine-tuning from our data) and b) a checklist or attestation we can attach to our DPA that lists the operational controls you have in place to ensure that (subprocessors, KV retention, export paths, audit logs).

To be explicit on the scope: this applies to all ingestion via the Redwood hosted API under our account (Halcyon AI, test and prod). We are willing to accept a technical addendum that documents the operational guarantees rather than changing core DPA language, but procurement wants proof we can produce a short evidence pack (subprocessor inventory, SOC2 artifacts, a short ops runbook) within 10 business days of contract sign.

Can you confirm what you can provide and any limitations (e.g., if you require a dedicated Dedicated or Private deployment for onshore KMS/residency)? Also attaching our draft DPA redlines for context.

Best,
Sophie
Sophie Turner | Head of Security & Compliance | Halcyon AI
attachment: Halcyon_DPA_redlines_v1.pdf

From: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@halcyon.ai>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 11 Sep 2028 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: initial ask: confirmation on no-model-learning and evidence pack

Hi Sophie — thanks for the clear list. Short answer: yes, we can commit to a no-model-learning ("no-train") policy for Halcyon AI under the hosted account you specify, and we can assemble an evidence pack to support that claim. A few operational clarifications up front so expectations are aligned: 

- Coverage: the commitment covers text generation, chat, embeddings, and reranking requests sent to the hosted Redwood API under your account id. It does not change model licensing or the model provider terms for open models themselves.
- Technical enforcement: we tag interactions at the request layer and prevent routing into model-improvement pipelines. For added separation we can enable ephemeral KV-only caching (prefix cache) and ensure no persistent capture to long-term training stores.
- Subprocessors: we will include a current subprocessor inventory. Note that some infra subprocessors (cloud provider managed services for telemetry and S3-like storage for nightly snapshots) are listed and may be updated on 30d notice — we can provide a snapshot at contract execution.
- Evidence pack contents we can deliver: subprocessor_inventory.csv, SOC 2 Type II scope summary, a 2-page ops runbook describing capture controls/retention, and a signed attestation template. If you need onshore KMS or guaranteed EU/US residency for retention, that is typically a Dedicated or Private deployment option — we can scope a plan and pricing.

I've looped in Kimberly (legal) and David (privacy/ops) to review the draft redlines and confirm the attestation language. We can produce the initial evidence pack in 7 business days after countersignature if nothing unexpected appears in redlines.

Next steps: Kimberly and David — can you review the Halcyon redlines and the requested attestation and advise on any gating DPA language? Sophie — would you accept an attestation addendum + evidence pack in lieu of the DPA language change?

Thanks,
Priyom
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai, Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@halcyon.ai>
Cc: david_kim@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 11 Sep 2028 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: initial ask: confirmation on no-model-learning and evidence pack

Sophie / team — quick legal read and proposed compromise: 

1) Contract language: instead of a broad "no training" covenant in the DPA body, propose a short addendum clause: "Redwood will not use Customer Content for model training or model improvement absent an explicit, separate written agreement." This keeps the DPA stable and provides the explicit legal promise you need.

2) Operational evidence: we will append an attestation (signed by Redwood VP Security) that lists current subprocessors, the capture/retention parameters for hosted accounts (default: ephemeral KV retention = 24 hours for prefix cache; request logs retained 30 days; audit trail 365 days), and the path for a dedicated onshore routing/KMS option. If Halcyon requires retention shorter than default or immediate deletion, operations will need to confirm feasibility; some telemetry (basic request/usage billing records) will remain for billing/audit purposes.

3) Subprocessor updates: we accept a 30-day notice clause for changes, and we commit to providing a snapshot used at time of execution as an exhibit to the DPA.

4) Escrow/exports: for exportability Halcyon can request a one-time export of processed interactions via SFTP/secure API. If you need recurring exports or escrow arrangements for derivative IP, that would be a separate engineering engagement and potentially a Dedicated offering.

Sophie — if that structure works we can prepare the addendum and the attestation template (attached) for signature.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Legal Counsel, Redwood Inference
attachment: no_train_attestation_template.docx

From: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@halcyon.ai>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@halcyon.ai>, procurement@halcyon.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 12 Sep 2028 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: initial ask: confirmation on no-model-learning and evidence pack

Kimberly / Priyom — that structure is acceptable to procurement and legal as a starting point. A couple of clarifications before we move to countersignature: 

- The attestation should explicitly state the enforcement mechanism ("tagging + exclusion from model-improvement pipelines") and the retention numbers you listed. Please include a short dated snapshot of the subprocessor inventory as an exhibit.
- Procurement expects the initial evidence pack within 7 business days of countersignature — we will plan for that. Please also include contact details for the ops lead responsible for evidence delivery so we can coordinate secure transfer (SFTP or DocuSign/ShareFile).
- For KMS/onshore residency: Halcyon will review the Dedicated offering pricing, but we want the DPA addendum and attestation first.

If Redwood can provide the signed attestation and the subprocessor snapshot (CSV) as part of the countersign package, procurement will greenlight speedier review. We can start the DocuSign envelope once we receive the addendum + attestation.

Thanks — Sophie
Sophie Turner | Head of Security & Compliance | Halcyon AI
